model: Lochinvar Armor, Knight, FTXL and Wall Mount via BASgatewayLX
applies_to: Lochinvar Knight (KB/KBX), Knight Wall Mount (WB), Armor (AW) and FTXL boilers and water heaters with SMART SYSTEM Modbus, read by a BASgatewayLX.
summary: Gateway profile shared by Lochinvar Knight, Wall Mount, Armor and FTXL units: 48 objects (13 AI, 7 AO, 16 BI, 12 BO), 29 polled by default. Inputs give the safety switches, flame, thermostat and contact states, pump and gas valve outputs, system/outlet/inlet/flue temperatures, firing rate and the status, blocking and lockout codes. The BMS command objects (room/tank thermostat, configuration bits, 0-10 V rate/setpoint command and BMS temperatures) are outputs but unpolled by default.
notes: Built from Contemporary Controls' BASgatewayLX Modbus device profile Lochinvar_WB__AW__KB__KBX_LX.csv; the profile maps the registers in the Lochinvar SMART SYSTEM Modbus communication document (https://www.ccontrols.com/support/dp/MODB-I-O.pdf).
Object instances are the ones this profile assigns when it is loaded into the gateway. A site that edited or rebuilt the profile may use different instances.
Only 29 of the 48 rows are flagged for polling in the profile; the rest are served only after you tick them in the gateway. Their descriptions say "not polled by default".

The CSV has no read/write column: Analog/Binary Inputs are read-only and Analog/Binary Outputs are commandable (priority array), which is how the gateway maps them (access inferred). Descriptions give the Modbus register each object reads.
Some names appear more than once in the profile as published (Room Thermostat 1; Room Thermostat 2; Tank Thermostat); they are kept as printed and told apart by instance.

integration.summary: Enable the configuration bits and command outputs you need, set the matching configuration bit (e.g. BO 36 for the rate/setpoint command), write the command, then read run-time contacts, outlet temperature, firing rate and the codes.

integration.enable: Each BMS value (enable/thermostat, rate/setpoint command, tank and system temperatures) only takes effect when its configuration bit (BO 34-41) is set; those and the command outputs are unpolled in the published profile.
setup: The BASgatewayLX presents each Modbus device as its own virtual BACnet device on BACnet IP; give it a unique device instance and Modbus address (serial) or IP address (Modbus TCP) when you add it with this profile.
One BASgatewayLX handles up to 100 Modbus devices and 1000 polled points in total, so leave unneeded rows unpolled.
gotchas: Command and configuration objects are unpolled by default; enable them first.
Unpolled rows do not appear as BACnet objects until enabled in the gateway's device profile page.
